steps.hint: Use two import statements: one for React and one for the CSS module file.

steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported React and the CSS module file.

steps.expectedOutcome: A functional component named CSSModuleDemo is created and returns null.
successCriteria: Component is named 'CSSModuleDemo' and returns null.

steps.title: Import CSS module styles object
steps.instruction: Import the CSS module styles object from the CSS file. Name the import 'styles'.
steps.hint: Use a named import from './App.module.css' to get the styles object.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing a CSS module
import styles from './MyComponent.module.css';
steps.expectedOutcome: The styles object is imported and ready to be used in the component.
successCriteria: The styles object is imported from './App.module.css' as 'styles'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported the CSS module styles object.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're importing from './App.module.css' and naming it 'styles'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import is missing or incorrect. You need to import the styles object from the CSS module file.

steps.title: Add basic JSX structure
steps.instruction: Return a simple div element from your CSSModuleDemo component.
steps.hint: Replace the current return statement with a JSX div element.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now returns a JSX div element instead of null.
successCriteria: The CSSModuleDemo component returns a JSX div element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added the basic JSX structure by returning a div element from your component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're returning a JSX div element from the component.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component should return a JSX div element. Check your return statement.

steps.title: Apply CSS module class to element
steps.instruction: In your component's JSX, add a className attribute to the <div> element and set it to styles.container to apply the CSS module class.
steps.hint: Use the imported styles object to access the CSS class name. The syntax is className={styles.container}.
steps.analogousExample:
// Applying a CSS module class to an element

Styled content
steps.expectedOutcome: The <div> element now has a className attribute that references the container class from the CSS module.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've successfully applied the CSS module class to the container element.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're using the imported styles object to access the container class.
steps.feedbackWrong: The className attribute should reference styles.container to apply the CSS module class.

element with the specified text inside the existing div element.

steps.expectedOutcome: The div element now contains both the heading and a paragraph with the specified text, demonstrating how CSS Modules can style nested content.
successCriteria: A paragraph element with the text 'This paragraph is styled using CSS Modules.' is added inside the div element that has the CSS module class applied.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added content to the styled element. The paragraph will inherit styles from the CSS module class applied to its parent div.
